confidence.rationale: The restaurant-controlled website and its linked Toast ordering surface confirm the Bethesda identity and reconcile all frozen items. Toast supplies current item-level allergen labels for many items, but several frozen allergen sets conflict with, or are unsupported by, the current labels; the official menu does not publish a complete allergen matrix.

sourceAttempts.notes: Restaurant-issued menus page was accessible and supplied the current restaurant menu.
The frozen Table22 Pasta Club URL resolved but exposed no usable product/menu content.
Official FAQ links to Toast; the ordering surface was accessible and provided current item-level allergen labels.
Targeted current search located indexed Toast item/menu pages, including Burger, Milanese, and Rigatoni Carbonara.
Third-party listing was available in current search results and corroborated the Bethesda menu identity.

findings.summary: Current Toast labels do not support the frozen allergen sets for Burger (frozen egg is absent), Ricotta (Toast labels gluten while frozen data only lists milk), Milanese (Toast additionally labels finfish), and Bucatini (current Toast label differs materially from frozen gluten/wheat claim). Chocolate Chip Cookies and Sourdough Bread have no item-level allergen label on the current Toast surface despite frozen allergen claims.
Aventino Pasta Club is absent from both current restaurant-issued menus and linked Toast ordering; its frozen Table22 product page exposed no usable current product content.
The Washington Post’s Best New Restaurants entry is an external press/interactive link from the restaurant home page, not a restaurant menu item.

The official FAQ asks guests to disclose allergies and says staff will try to accommodate them, but it does not provide a cross-contact or shared-equipment policy. Toast displays a non-guaranteed special-request advisory.

summary: Aventino Cucina Bethesda is confirmed. All 19 frozen audit items were reconciled exactly once: 17 remain represented on current official or restaurant-linked menu surfaces, Aventino Pasta Club is stale, and the Washington Post link is an extraction artifact. Current Toast allergen labeling creates material discrepancies for six frozen allergen records, so this result requires coordinator/Sol review rather than terminal verification.
coordinatorNotes: Do not treat unlabelled Toast items as allergen-free; the official FAQ directs guests to disclose allergies but provides no cross-contact guarantee.
The Toast menu is seasonal and item availability/ingredient descriptions differ from the restaurant menu page; capture fresh evidence before any repair.
Review allergen normalization for source label Gluten versus frozen gluten+wheat before applying any change.
